answer: Panels hide canaries whose labels sit in a protocol vault, and each seat gets a uniquely watermarked variant, so a cached judgment cannot serve two clones. A crystal canary has an undisputed grade, letting the protocol score evaluators independently; accuracy gates voting weight. Canaries are sparse, drawn after assignment from a tundra of near-duplicates, so they cannot be spotted early or pooled. A farm must run real evaluation on every clone to retain its weight, since borrowed answers fail the watermark. Per-clone cost stays non-poolable while honest evaluators accumulate influence.
